title: Canonical normalization data for the point tensor system
statement: Fix a finite-field datum $D$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, an algebraic closure $\Omega/\mathbf Q_\ell$, and a simultaneous point tensor system $S$ as in [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], [def-sf-point-fibre-tensor-system], [def-sf-point-fibre-tensor-finite-models], [def-sf-point-fibre-tensor-models], [def-sf-point-fibre-tensor-reduction], [def-sf-point-fibre-tensor-rational-compatibility], [def-sf-point-fibre-tensor-common-stage], [def-sf-point-finite-source-constraints], [def-sf-point-integral-scalar-square]. Define the type $\operatorname{Canonical}(S)$ of data with the following fields, with the coefficient fields, indices and embeddings specified in each field: (1) finite source associators and unitors are the recorded restrictions; (2) finite tensor comparisons are normalized on K-flat models; (3) integral comparisons have the full two-coordinate Roos normalization; (4) every quotient reduction square, including equal indices, commutes; (5) integral scalar-extension squares are the specified scalarTensorChain squares; (6) for every field $E$ in the carrier universe, with no finite-extension or $\mathbf Q_\ell$-algebra requirement, coefficient and carrier lift tensor data have the pure-tensor normalization; (7) fraction-field localization has its canonical scalar tensor data; (8) its counit equals the exact-functor localization comparison; (9) rational tensor comparisons are the localized integral comparisons; (10) rational units come from those same integral units; (11) every extension between finite coefficient fields has the specified derived scalar tensor data; (12) its counit is the exact coefficient-functor comparison; (13) rational cross-field squares commute using these data; (14) extension from each finite coefficient stage to $\Omega$ has scalar tensor data; (15) its counit is the specified exact-functor comparison; (16) the closed-coefficient tensor comparison is normalized at every common finite stage; and (17) its unit is scalar extension of the actual rational unit. This is a type of specified normalization data, not an assertion that such data exist.
